purpose: How a tax preparation practice moves one return from acceptance to accepted acknowledgment at peak-season speed without losing accuracy: what each stage gate must prove before work advances, which error class each control actually catches, what the workpaper and due-diligence record must contain, how an unclear item is researched, escalated, extended or declined instead of guessed, and how the most sensitive client data class a small practice ever holds is protected from intake through destruction.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
the practice is a small independent preparation practice earning per-return fees on individual and small-business returns, with a compressed filing peak and a thinner off-season tail

preparer registration, electronic-filing credentialing and any state preparer requirements are prerequisites already held before the season; they are treated here as binding constraints on the workflow, not as content this KB re-derives, and their current requirements must be verified in the practice's own jurisdiction

rules, forms, thresholds, deadlines, penalty exposure and record-retention periods change every filing year, so every regulatory reference in this KB names a class of obligation rather than asserting a current requirement
returns are prepared in commercial preparation software with electronic filing as the default path and paper filing as a documented exception

where a step says 'second person', a solo practice substitutes a scheduled self-review at a separate sitting against the same written checklist, and 'escalate' means a paid outside credentialed reviewer rather than a colleague down the hall
client-supplied information is relied on without audit but never without inquiry: an answer that conflicts with a document already in the file triggers a question and a recorded resolution
exclusions: preparer credential and registration classes, electronic-filing infrastructure, and preparation-software selection and setup - the practice-setup sibling KB owns those; this KB only treats them as constraints the workflow must respect

choosing a client segment (individual, small-business, niche), choosing a service model (office, virtual, hybrid), the seasonal demand curve as an economic mechanism, and pricing architecture by return complexity - all sibling practice-setup territory
what makes clients return annually, post-season follow-up, next-year positioning, referral growth and any other retention mechanism - sibling returning-client KB territory

off-season revenue lines as revenue (extension-season work, amendments as an offer, quarterly estimate service, planning-adjacent education, bookkeeping cross-over) and year-round capacity smoothing - sibling territory; this KB treats an extension only as an in-pipeline quality decision and an amendment only as the correction path for a discovered error
any statement of what a specific jurisdiction's rules, thresholds, deadlines, penalty amounts, credit eligibility tests or retention periods currently are
the correct tax treatment of any specific client fact pattern, and any personalized tax, legal or financial advice
representation before a tax authority, beyond naming it as a credential-bound obligation class and an engagement-scope exclusion
bookkeeping and write-up production, entity formation, and any audit or attest engagement
refund-size, speed or comparative-outcome claims in marketing or in the chair, in any form

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RETURN_PIPELINE_CHARTER names the stages and a definition of done that ends at recorded acknowledgment plus a complete retained file, and COMPLETENESS_GATE shows what must be true before preparation may begin

competency_questions.question: Which client questions may we answer ourselves, and which have to be researched, escalated or referred out?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ADVICE_SCOPE_BOUNDARY gives the two-column classification and the routing wording, and AMBIGUITY_TRIAGE_PROTOCOL gives the decision procedure that routes the advice-side question

competency_questions.question: What do we say to a client who wants a bigger refund, compares us to the shop that 'got them more', or pushes a position the documents do not support?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: OUTCOME_PROMISE_CONDUCT_RULE supplies the no-promise standard, the fee-basis conduct class, the pressure script and the vulnerable-client handling, and CLIENT_REVIEW_CONVERSATION shows where it is applied verbatim

competency_questions.question: Which returns do we take this season, which do we decline or refer, and what does the signed engagement actually cover?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ENGAGEMENT_ACCEPTANCE_AND_SCOPE states the competence, capacity, records and posture tests and lists what the engagement letter must fix in writing, including the exclusions

competency_questions.question: How do we know a client's document set is complete before anyone starts preparing?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PRIOR_YEAR_BASELINE supplies the expected-document list and the carryforward inventory, DOCUMENT_REQUEST_ORGANIZER turns it into a tracked request loop, and COMPLETENESS_GATE defines the disposition required for every expected-but-absent item

competency_questions.question: How do client documents and identifiers get in, get stored, and get destroyed without exposing the household, and what do we do when we are phished or impersonated?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CLIENT_DATA_SECURITY_BASELINE names the safeguards obligation class with a verify-locally requirement and an incident path, SECURE_DOC_INTAKE_CHANNEL fixes the single indexed receiving channel and the conversion path for insecure deliveries, and FILE_RETENTION_AND_DISPOSAL covers destruction

competency_questions.question: How do we get more returns out the door in the peak weeks without accuracy falling as volume rises?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RETURN_QUEUE_TRIAGE gives the state machine, the work-in-progress cap and the batching mechanism, RETURN_PIPELINE_CHARTER supplies the never-touch-it-twice ordering principle, and REVIEW_TIER_ASSIGNMENT shows how review depth is allocated rather than skipped

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ERROR_CLASS_TAXONOMY names each error class with its owning stage and catching control, SOFTWARE_DIAGNOSTIC_CONTROLS states what the software can and cannot see, and REVIEW_PASS_EXECUTION works the taxonomy as its checklist

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DUE_DILIGENCE_DOCUMENTATION names the obligation class with a verify-locally flag and lists the four parts of the record, and PREPARATION_WORKPAPER_STANDARD shows where those parts live in the workpapers

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: AMBIGUITY_TRIAGE_PROTOCOL gives the ordered procedure and forbids filing on assumption, SOURCE_AUTHORITY_LADDER ranks what may be relied on for the filing year in question, and EXTENSION_DECISION_RULE supplies the extend branch

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REVIEW_TIER_ASSIGNMENT states the risk signals that set the tier and the raise-only rule, and REVIEW_PASS_EXECUTION lists the checks and the recorded sign-off the pass must produce

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CLIENT_REVIEW_CONVERSATION defines the walkthrough and its closing omission question, and SIGNATURE_AUTH_AND_EFILE fixes authorization after finalization, the signing-preparer obligation class, acknowledgment as the filing test and the reject handling path

competency_questions.question: What must remain in the file after filing, how long does it live, and what do we do when we find an error or a notice lands?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FILE_RETENTION_AND_DISPOSAL lists the closed-file contents and names retention and disposal as obligation classes to verify locally, and ERROR_DISCLOSURE_AND_CORRECTION fixes the disclosure-first behaviour, the correction options and the notice triage

competency_questions.question: How does the practice learn from the errors this season produced instead of repeating them next season?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DEFECT_LOG_CONTROL_TUNING defines what is logged at the moment of catch, the stage-of-origin versus stage-of-catch reading, and the off-season revision cycle, using ERROR_CLASS_TAXONOMY as its vocabulary

glossary.definition: The entry check that stops a return from being started until every document expected from the prior-year baseline has a disposition (arrived, confirmed not applicable with the client's stated reason, or still outstanding) and the change questions are answered in writing.

The preparer's mark that a specific figure on the return traces to a specific source document, and conversely that every source document received was entered somewhere; the practice's cheapest defence against transcription and omission errors.

The internal record behind the return: the document index, the tie-out marks, the client questions and answers, and a note for each judgment call stating the fact assumed, the document supporting it, the authority rung reached and who decided.

A figure whose only source is the prior-year file rather than a current-year document - loss and credit carryovers, basis and at-risk amounts, depreciation schedules and accumulated amounts, overpayments applied forward, and prior elections - and therefore the class most often lost at rollover or at a change of preparer.

The evidence set a paid preparer must be able to produce for credits and statuses that carry a due-diligence obligation: the eligibility questions asked, the client's answers, the documents provided or described, and the contemporaneous note resolving anything inconsistent. Scope, forms and retention differ by jurisdiction and must be verified currently.

The ranked list of what a preparer may rely on for an unclear item - statute and regulations, then official agency guidance and the filing year's official instructions and publications, then vendor-cited authority, then reputable professional analysis - with forum posts, social media and 'my last preparer did it this way' excluded from the ladder entirely.

The depth of review assigned to a return before it is prepared, running from documented self-check, through second-person review, to full credentialed review of return, workpapers and authority notes; raisable by anyone, lowerable only by the credentialed reviewer.

The signed taxpayer authorization class that permits the practice to transmit a specific finished return electronically; it is obtained after the return is final, re-obtained when the return changes materially, and retained as part of the closed file under a retention class that must be verified locally.

The electronic acceptance record returned after transmission; until it is received and logged against the client file the return is transmitted but not filed, which is why 'sent' is never the practice's definition of done.

A return formally placed in a waiting-on-client or waiting-on-decision state with a named blocker, an owner and an age, so that incomplete work is visible and ageing on the board rather than sitting half-prepared in someone's stack.

nodes.definition: Fix one prepared return as the practice's unit of production and name the stages it must pass in order: acceptance and signed scope, prior-year baseline, document request, completeness gate, preparation, ambiguity resolution where needed, review at an assigned tier, client walkthrough, signed authorization, transmission, recorded acknowledgment, closed file. The charter's real work is the definition of done - a return is finished when its acceptance acknowledgment is logged and its file is complete, never when it is 'sent' and never when the client has been told a number - and the ordering principle that the practice's peak-season throughput comes from touching each return the fewest possible times, not from compressing steps. It therefore states up front that a return which cannot satisfy the gate in front of it is parked or extended rather than pushed forward, and that every downstream node in this KB exists to make one gate provable.

included: the ordered stage list for one return
the definition of done ending at logged acknowledgment plus complete file
the park-or-extend rule when a gate cannot be met
the touch-it-once throughput principle
excluded: how many returns the practice should take in a season and at what price
the seasonal demand curve as an economic mechanism
off-season service lines

pros.claim: A written definition of done stops the two most expensive silent failures - a transmitted return nobody confirmed and a filed return with no file behind it
pros.example: the season-end reconciliation of transmitted returns against logged acknowledgments becomes a routine check instead of a discovery in June

pros.claim: Naming the stages makes 'where is this return' answerable by anyone in the office in seconds
pros.example: a client calling on a Saturday gets 'it is in review, assigned tier two, back to you Monday' rather than a promise to look for the folder

cons.claim: A stage model invites ceremony: a solo practice can spend more time recording stage transitions than preparing
cons.example: a one-preparer office updating five status fields for a straightforward wage-income return

cons.claim: A rigid pipeline resists the genuinely odd return that needs its stages resequenced
cons.example: a client who must file in a hurry to satisfy a lender, where the walkthrough happens before some peripheral documents arrive

failure_modes: treating transmission as the end of the return so acknowledgment tracking is nobody's job
letting the charter exist as a wall poster while the actual queue runs on folder height
defining stages without gates, so the model describes the work but never stops it
acceptance_tests: the stage list, the gate for each stage and the definition of done are written down and used by the queue board rather than remembered
every transmitted return in the season reconciles to a logged acknowledgment or an open reject with an owner
revisit_triggers: a return type recurs that the stage list cannot represent
a season ends with returns that were transmitted but never confirmed
the practice adds staff, a second location or a virtual intake path that changes who owns which stage

base.update_signal: a season's reconciliation showing transmitted-but-unacknowledged returns, or a recurring return type whose real path does not match the charted stages

nodes.definition: Keep a standing two-column classification of everything clients ask, because the questions that cross the line arrive casually, mid-appointment, from someone who trusts you. Preparation-side work is what the practice performs: collecting and reading source documents, entering them and tying each figure to its document, applying rules whose application to documented facts is not in dispute, explaining what a line of the return says and which document produced it, and telling a client what is missing. Advice-side questions require researched or credentialed judgment and are routed rather than answered on the spot - whether an activity is a business or a hobby, worker classification, entity structure and elections, multi-state residency positions, basis and retirement decisions, what the client should do before year end, and any prior-year position someone else took. Routing means one of three visible things: researched under the authority ladder, escalated to the practice's credentialed reviewer, or referred to an outside credentialed advisor or attorney - and the client is told which. The node also names preparer registration and credential classes, and the representation privileges that ride on them, as prerequisites whose current requirements must be verified in the practice's own jurisdiction rather than copied from a message board, and states that this KB is process knowledge, not a position on anyone's facts.

included: the two-column classification of incoming questions
the three visible routing outcomes and the wording that delivers them
the credential and representation obligation class with a verify-locally requirement
how the boundary constrains what goes in writing to a client
excluded: what any jurisdiction's credential rules currently require
obtaining or maintaining the credentials themselves, which the practice-setup KB owns
the correct treatment of any specific client's facts

pros.claim: A prepared classification makes the redirect fast and consistent instead of improvised under a client's expectant silence
pros.example: a client asking mid-appointment whether they should switch to an S corporation next year gets the same routed answer from the front desk preparer as from the owner

pros.claim: Routing rather than refusing keeps the practice useful and keeps the relationship, which is what makes the boundary survivable
pros.example: the preparer writes the fact pattern down, books the credentialed reviewer's off-season slot, and the client leaves with a date instead of a shrug

cons.claim: Clients read the boundary as evasiveness when the question feels obvious to them
cons.example: an owner irritated that 'can I deduct my truck' becomes a documented question rather than a yes

cons.claim: The line moves with credential, jurisdiction and engagement, so the classification needs local verification and periodic review rather than being settled once
cons.example: a practice taking its first client in a neighbouring state discovering the preparer rules there differ from the ones it has always worked under

failure_modes: answering an advice-side question casually because it was asked casually
putting an off-the-cuff treatment in an email where it reads as the practice's written position
assuming another jurisdiction's rules apply locally instead of verifying them
using the boundary as a way to avoid work the practice is in fact engaged to do
acceptance_tests: every question class the practice actually meets is written on the preparation side or the advice side, with routing wording attached to the advice side
no client-facing message states a treatment for an advice-side question without an authority rung and a named decision-maker behind it
credential, registration and representation content names the obligation class and instructs local verification rather than asserting a current rule
revisit_triggers: a question arrives that fits neither column
the practice adds a jurisdiction, a return type or a credentialed staff member
a client acts on something a preparer said in passing and it turns out to be wrong

base.update_signal: a locally verified change in preparer credential or representation rules, a new jurisdiction or return type, or a client question class that neither column covers

nodes.definition: Bind the practice's conduct to a disclosure-first standard that survives the busiest week of the season. No promise or implication of a refund amount before a return is prepared; no comparative claim that the practice gets people more back than another preparer; no fee quoted or scaled on the size of a refund, which is a fee-basis conduct class restricted or prohibited in many regimes and must be verified locally; and no position taken because a client asked for it, threatened to leave, or reported that a friend's preparer allows it. Fees are quoted on complexity and the outcome is described as whatever the client's documented facts produce. When a client pushes, the response is scripted and repeatable: here is what the documents support, here is precisely what would have to be true and documented for a different result, here is how you could obtain that documentation, and here is your option to take the return elsewhere - with the practice's position stated in writing and no argument about the number. Vulnerable-client care is part of the same rule rather than a courtesy: elderly clients, clients with limited English or literacy, first-time filers, the recently bereaved and clients in financial distress get slower explanation, no add-on pressure, a check that they understood what they are attesting to, and extra care around refund-transfer or advance products whose costs must be disclosed plainly before anything is signed.

included: the no-outcome-promise standard and the fee-basis conduct class flag
the scripted response to outcome pressure and to aggressive-position requests
vulnerable-client handling inside the preparation and delivery conversation
plain disclosure of any ancillary product's cost before signature
excluded: the practice's pricing architecture and how complexity tiers are priced, which the practice-setup KB owns
marketing channels and client acquisition
what any jurisdiction's advertising or fee rules currently say

pros.claim: A scripted refusal that offers a documented path keeps the conversation calm and keeps the practice's signature clean
pros.example: a client convinced their mileage can be estimated leaves with a log template and a re-quote date rather than an argument or an unsupported deduction

pros.claim: Refusing outcome-based selling protects the practice against the exact client mix that produces notices, disputes and unpaid rework
pros.example: the walk-in who opens with 'how big a refund can you get me' self-selects out before becoming a file with an unprovable claim

cons.claim: The rule costs visible revenue in the peak weeks when a competitor down the street will say yes
cons.example: a returning client leaving because another office agreed to claim a dependent the file cannot support

cons.claim: Slower, careful handling of vulnerable clients consumes exactly the capacity that peak season has least of
cons.example: a forty-minute walkthrough for a bereaved first-time filer in the last week before the deadline

failure_modes: softening the script under a long-standing client's disappointment
letting a preparer quote a fee 'out of the refund' as a convenience
selling an ancillary product to a distressed client without stating its cost in plain terms
treating the rule as a front-desk policy rather than something the preparer applies at the walkthrough
acceptance_tests: no client-facing material, script or conversation states or implies a refund amount, a comparative outcome, or a fee tied to refund size
the pressure script exists in writing and every preparer can deliver it without improvising a position
for any ancillary product offered, the client's file records that the cost was disclosed in plain terms before signature
revisit_triggers: a preparer reports being talked into a position by a client
a client complaint or review alleges a promised outcome
the practice adds an ancillary product or a new fee arrangement

base.update_signal: a complaint alleging a promised outcome, a locally verified change in fee-basis or advertising conduct rules, or a preparer reporting they conceded a position under client pressure

nodes.definition: Rank what a preparer is allowed to rely on when a treatment is unclear, and require the file to record the highest rung actually reached. The ladder runs from statute and regulations, to official agency guidance and the filing year's own form instructions and publications, to the preparation software's cited authority (useful as a pointer, never as the citation itself), to reputable professional-body or paid research-service analysis - and explicitly excludes forum answers, social posts, a colleague's recollection, a client's 'my last preparer did it this way' and last year's notes reused without checking. The second half of the node is currency: tax rules are annual, provisions expire and thresholds move, so a source counts only if it is the version for the filing year at issue, and any conclusion carried forward from a previous season must be re-verified against the current year's instructions before it is reused. What lands in the workpapers is a short conclusion note in fixed form - the question as a fact pattern, the fact that would change the answer, the rung reached, the citation or instruction reference, the date checked and who decided.

included: the ranked list of usable sources and the excluded ones
the filing-year currency requirement and the re-verification rule for carried-forward conclusions
the fixed form of the conclusion note in the workpapers
excluded: the substantive answer to any tax question
which research subscription a practice should buy
training curricula and continuing-education planning

pros.claim: A ranked ladder converts 'I think it works this way' into a recorded, checkable position that a reviewer or a notice response can stand on
pros.example: a home-office question resolved against the filing year's own instructions and noted with the date checked, instead of against a half-remembered thread

pros.claim: The currency rule catches the quiet failure mode of a practice that has done something the same way for years
pros.example: a recurring credit whose eligibility conditions changed for the filing year being re-checked because the note says re-verify before reuse

cons.claim: Climbing the ladder costs peak-season minutes the practice does not have, which is why the protocol above it must timebox the climb
cons.example: twenty minutes of instruction reading on a question worth a small figure on one return

cons.claim: Primary sources answer narrowly and often leave the client's actual fact pattern unresolved, which pushes the item to escalation rather than settling it
cons.example: instructions that address the ordinary case and say nothing about the client's mixed-use situation

failure_modes: citing the software's help text as if it were authority
reusing a prior-season conclusion without re-checking it against the current year
recording a conclusion with no rung, no date and no decision-maker
researching indefinitely instead of escalating when the ladder does not resolve the fact pattern
acceptance_tests: every judgment note in a closed file names the rung reached, the reference, the date checked and the person who decided
no file records a forum post, a social media source or a colleague's recollection as the basis of a position
conclusions reused from a prior season carry a current-year re-verification date
revisit_triggers: a new filing year's instructions and publications are released
a position the practice has reused for several seasons is questioned by a notice or a reviewer
the practice changes research subscription or preparation software

base.update_signal: release of the filing year's instructions and publications, a notice challenging a long-reused position, or a change of research source or software vendor

nodes.definition: Treat the client file as the most sensitive data class a small practice will ever hold - full legal names, taxpayer identification numbers, dates of birth for a whole household including children, bank routing and account details, employer and income records, sometimes immigration or custody documents - and stand up the safeguards obligation class that applies to paid preparers: a written information security program with a named responsible person, unique credentials and multi-factor authentication on the electronic-filing and portal accounts, encryption in transit and at rest, least-privilege access so seasonal staff see only their own clients, locked storage and a clean-desk rule for paper, documented vendor and cloud due-diligence, training before a seasonal hire touches a file, and a written incident path that includes the breach-notification and preparer-account-compromise reporting classes. The specifics of every one of those obligations differ by jurisdiction and change; the class is named here and its current content must be verified locally. The node also holds the season's live threats, because they are operational rather than theoretical: messages impersonating the software vendor or the agency to harvest e-file credentials, a client-lookalike email asking to change refund deposit details late in the process, staff devices used at home, and seasonal access that outlives the season.

included: the safeguards program obligation class and its named components
access control for seasonal staff and device handling
the live seasonal threat list and the incident and notification path as classes
vendor and cloud due-diligence for portal and preparation software
excluded: what any jurisdiction's security or notification rules currently require in detail
which specific security product to buy
the practice's software and e-file infrastructure selection, owned by the practice-setup KB

pros.claim: A written program with a named owner turns security from an intention into a checkable list before the season loads
pros.example: multi-factor authentication verified on the e-file account and the portal in the pre-season checklist rather than after an incident

pros.claim: Least-privilege and end-of-season access removal contain the damage of the most likely incident, which is credential compromise rather than a sophisticated attack
pros.example: a seasonal preparer's account disabled the week the season ends, so a later credential leak reaches nothing

cons.claim: Every control adds friction exactly where clients and seasonal staff are least tolerant of it
cons.example: an older client abandoning a portal upload and arriving with paper because the identity verification step defeated them

cons.claim: A small practice cannot fully verify a vendor's security claims and inherits risk it can only document, not control
cons.example: a cloud storage or portal provider whose own breach exposes files the practice never mishandled

failure_modes: reusing credentials across the e-file account, the portal and email
letting documents arrive by ordinary email because the client finds it easier
leaving seasonal staff access active after the season
having no written incident path, so the first hour of a real incident is spent deciding who decides
acceptance_tests: a written information security program exists, names a responsible person, and was reviewed before the season opened
multi-factor authentication is verified on the electronic-filing account, the portal and practice email, and access lists are reconciled at season end
the incident path names the first three actions, the notification obligation classes to check, and who contacts clients
no client identifiers are stored or transmitted outside the approved indexed channel
revisit_triggers: any phishing attempt, credential compromise or vendor breach notice
a change of portal, storage or preparation software vendor
hiring seasonal staff or adding remote work
a locally verified change in the safeguards or notification obligation classes

base.update_signal: an incident or attempted compromise, a vendor breach notice, a locally verified change in the safeguards or breach-notification obligation classes, or a change in staffing or remote-access arrangements

nodes.definition: Decide deliberately, before any work, whether this particular return is one the practice will prepare this season, and record the answer in a signed engagement letter. Acceptance turns on four tests applied in order: competence - does the return contain forms, entity types and situations the practice has actually prepared and reviewed before; capacity - can it be finished properly at this point in the calendar or does it enter on the extension path; records - can the client produce substantiation for what they intend to claim; and posture - does the client accept that the return will reflect their documented facts rather than a target. Declining or referring is a normal, cheap outcome here and an expensive one at any later stage. The engagement letter then fixes the return years and jurisdictions in scope, what is excluded (bookkeeping and cleanup, prior-year returns, amendments, audit or notice representation, planning engagements, entity returns), the fee basis and what triggers a re-quote, the client's responsibility to supply complete and accurate information and to retain substantiation, the practice's reliance on that information without audit, the documents-in deadline for the peak wave, and the conditions under which the practice will not sign a return.

included: the four acceptance tests and the decline-or-refer outcome
the contents the engagement letter must fix, including exclusions and the will-not-sign conditions
the documents-in deadline that separates the peak wave from the extension path
the written change requirement for scope expansion mid-engagement
excluded: which client segment the practice should serve at all
how the fee is calculated and what complexity tiers cost
the marketing and intake funnel that produced the enquiry

pros.claim: Screening before work turns a bad return into a five-minute conversation instead of a season-long problem
pros.example: a first-time enquiry involving a foreign account and a partnership interest referred out in the initial call rather than discovered in preparation

pros.claim: A written scope with named exclusions is what makes 'that is a separate engagement' a fact rather than an argument
pros.example: a client asking mid-season for last year's return to be amended receives a written change order rather than free rework

cons.claim: Screening rejects revenue in the weeks the practice feels busiest and richest, which makes the discipline hardest exactly when it matters
cons.example: declining a complex new client in early February whose fee would have been the largest of the month

cons.claim: Acceptance criteria applied mechanically can screen out learning work the practice should take on deliberately with a reviewer attached
cons.example: refusing every first rental-property return and never developing the capability

failure_modes: accepting on the client's description of the return rather than on the documents they can produce
starting work before the engagement letter is signed because the client is in a hurry
expanding scope verbally and discovering at billing that nobody agreed a fee
treating the acceptance tests as a form to complete rather than a decision to make
acceptance_tests: no preparation begins on a return without a signed engagement letter for that year in the file
each acceptance decision records which of the four tests it turned on, including for declines and referrals
the engagement letter states exclusions, the will-not-sign conditions and the documents-in deadline in plain language
revisit_triggers: a return type repeatedly costs far more effort than its acceptance assessment predicted
the practice gains or loses a capability or a credentialed reviewer
a scope dispute reaches billing or a complaint

base.update_signal: a season's effort data showing an accepted return type consistently exceeding its assessed complexity, a scope dispute at billing, or a change in the practice's capability set

nodes.definition: Build every current-year return on top of a reconstructed prior-year baseline rather than a blank organizer, because the prior return is simultaneously the best completeness checklist the practice will ever have, the only source of items that exist nowhere else, and its earliest error detector. The baseline extracts four things: the inventory of income and deduction document types that appeared last year, so that the absence of one this year becomes an active question rather than a silence; the household picture - filing status, dependents, ages that matter, jurisdictions filed; the carryforward inventory, whose values live only in the prior file (loss and credit carryovers, basis and at-risk figures, depreciation schedules with accumulated amounts and remaining lives, overpayment applied forward, elections made); and the recurring judgment items with the position the prior preparer took. For a returning client this is a rollover check that the software's own carryover must be reconciled against, not trusted blindly. For a new client it is real work performed before preparation - obtaining the prior return and any depreciation schedules from the client at intake, not at review - and where the prior return is unavailable or visibly wrong, the baseline forces an explicit decision to reconstruct, to limit scope in writing, or to decline.

included: the expected-document inventory drawn from last year
the carryforward inventory and the reconciliation of software rollover against the prior return
the new-client path for obtaining prior returns and depreciation schedules
the decision forced when the prior year is missing or wrong
excluded: preparing or amending the prior-year return itself, which is a separate engagement
judging the prior preparer's competence to the client
the retention rules for the prior-year file

pros.claim: The prior return converts omission from an invisible failure into a listed open question
pros.example: a brokerage document that appeared last year and has not arrived this year becomes an item on the chase list instead of a gap nobody notices until a matching notice arrives

pros.claim: Carryforward items caught at baseline are caught at the only moment they are cheap
pros.example: a depreciation schedule obtained at intake rather than reconstructed during review week from a client's incomplete records

cons.claim: The prior year anchors the preparer to last year's answers, including its mistakes and its stale positions
cons.example: a classification the previous preparer chose being carried forward because it was there, without being re-checked against the current year's rules

cons.claim: Reconstructing a baseline for a new client is unpaid-feeling work at the busiest moment
cons.example: chasing a new client's former preparer for a depreciation schedule while the peak queue builds

failure_modes: trusting the software's carryover without reconciling it to the prior return
accepting a new client without the prior-year return and discovering the gap at review
carrying forward a prior position without re-verifying it for the filing year
treating the baseline as data entry rather than as the completeness checklist
acceptance_tests: every return has a documented expected-document list derived from the prior year before the document request goes out
every carryforward figure on the return traces to the prior-year return or a schedule in the file, not to the software alone
for a new client, the prior-year return and any depreciation schedules are in the file, or the file records the reconstruct, limit-scope or decline decision
revisit_triggers: the client reports a life change that makes last year's document set unrepresentative
software rollover is found to have dropped or duplicated a figure
a new client's prior return proves unobtainable or unreliable

base.update_signal: a rollover defect found in the software, a client life change that invalidates last year's document pattern, or an omission error whose root cause traces to a baseline that was never built

nodes.definition: Send each client a request built from their own baseline and known changes rather than a generic checklist, and run it as a tracked loop instead of a hopeful email. The request names each expected document by its form family and the employer, payer or institution it came from last year, so the client is looking for something specific rather than deciding what counts. Beside it sits the short set of change questions that actually move a return - marriage, separation or a death in the household; a birth, an adoption, a dependent who started working or moved out, or support arrangements that changed; a move or work in another state; a new self-employment, gig or rental income stream; buying or selling a home; retirement account distributions and rollovers; education costs; health-coverage documents; digital-asset activity; foreign accounts or income - each phrased as a question a non-specialist can answer. The request states the practice's documents-in deadline for the peak wave and what happens after it. The chase loop then gives every outstanding item an owner, a last-contact date and an escalation from message to call, so that 'waiting on the client' is a visible state with an age rather than a belief held by one preparer.

included: the personalized expected-document list and the change questions
the documents-in deadline statement and its consequence
the chase loop with owner, age and escalation path
excluded: advising the client on what any answer to a change question means for their tax position
the retention or security handling of what arrives, which the intake channel and security nodes own
off-season client communication and next-year positioning

pros.claim: Naming the payer and form family collapses the round trips that a generic checklist guarantees
pros.example: asking for the year-end statement from the specific brokerage that issued one last year, rather than for 'any investment documents'

pros.claim: A tracked chase loop with ages converts the season's biggest hidden cost into a visible list that can be worked in batches
pros.example: a Monday call block that clears eleven aged items instead of eleven interruptions across the week

cons.claim: Personalized requests cost preparation time per client before any billable work starts
cons.example: building tailored requests for a whole returning base in January while the first wave is already arriving

cons.claim: Long change-question lists depress response rates, so the set must stay short enough to be answered rather than complete enough to be safe
cons.example: a two-page questionnaire that comes back blank while a six-question version comes back filled

failure_modes: sending the same generic organizer to every client and calling intake done
letting chase items live in one preparer's memory or inbox
asking change questions the client cannot answer without advice, then accepting a guess
collecting answers verbally and never writing them into the file
acceptance_tests: each client's request names expected documents by form family and source rather than by generic category
every outstanding item has an owner, a last-contact date and a next action
change-question answers are recorded in the file in the client's own words
revisit_triggers: response rates or round-trip counts worsen against the prior season
a defect log entry traces an omission back to a question that was never asked
a new document type or reporting form becomes common in the client base

base.update_signal: season-over-season change in round trips per return or in response rate, or a logged omission traced to a missing change question

nodes.definition: Run every document through one indexed receiving channel - a secure portal or encrypted upload tied to an identity-verified client account - and treat the convenient alternatives as exceptions that must be converted rather than tolerated: ordinary email attachments, photographs sent by text, and paper left at the front desk each get a documented conversion path that lands the item in the index and destroys the insecure copy, with the client told once, politely, why. Each received item is named to a fixed convention (client, tax year, form family, source, received date), logged against the outstanding request list so completeness can be computed instead of guessed, and checked on arrival for four things: legibility, the right taxpayer, the right tax year, and whether it supersedes an earlier version as a corrected or amended document. Paper drop-offs get a written receipt and a scan-then-return rule, so the practice never becomes the custodian of a client's only copy of anything, and the front desk never holds a stack of unlabelled identifiers over a weekend.

included: the single indexed channel and the conversion path for insecure deliveries
the naming convention and the arrival checks
paper receipt, scanning and return handling
excluded: choosing and contracting the portal product itself
the wider safeguards program and incident response, held by the security baseline node
reading the documents for preparation purposes

pros.claim: One indexed channel is what makes the completeness gate computable rather than a preparer's impression
pros.example: the outstanding list showing three items open for a client because arrivals were logged, not remembered

pros.claim: Arrival checks catch wrong-year and superseded documents before they become a wrong return or an amendment
pros.example: a corrected year-end statement recognised as superseding the original at intake rather than after transmission

cons.claim: Insisting on the channel loses documents from clients who will simply not use a portal
cons.example: an older client who mails paper and does not answer portal invitations, forcing a manual conversion path every year

cons.claim: Indexing every arrival is real clerical load at the exact moment arrivals peak
cons.example: a February day where document arrivals outrun the person naming and logging them, and the index falls behind the pile

failure_modes: accepting emailed identifiers because refusing feels rude, and never converting or deleting them
storing arrivals without logging them against the request list, so completeness reverts to guesswork
missing that a document is a corrected version of one already entered
holding a client's only original paper document
acceptance_tests: every document in a client file carries the naming convention and a received date logged against the request list
no client identifiers remain in ordinary email or messaging after the conversion path has run
paper received is receipted, scanned and returned or destroyed per the schedule, with nothing held as a sole copy
revisit_triggers: clients repeatedly bypass the channel
a corrected document is discovered after preparation started
the portal or storage vendor changes

base.update_signal: a rise in out-of-channel deliveries, a corrected-document miss found downstream, or a change of portal or storage vendor

nodes.definition: Refuse to start preparation until the received set reconciles to the expected set and the change questions are answered, because a return begun incomplete is a return touched three or four times, reviewed against a moving target, and finished in the week when there is least room for it. The gate is a comparison, not a feeling: every expected item from the baseline carries a disposition - arrived and indexed, confirmed not applicable this year with the client's stated reason recorded, or still outstanding with an owner - and the return may not enter preparation while any item sits in the third state without an explicit, documented decision to proceed without it. The gate also requires the change-question answers in writing, and flags before preparation, not after, any item that will carry a due-diligence obligation class so the questions are asked while the client is still engaged in the conversation. A return failing the gate moves to the parked state with a named blocker and an age; past the season's documents-in cutoff, a parked return converts to the extension path automatically rather than competing for peak capacity with returns that are ready.

included: the expected-versus-received reconciliation and the three dispositions
the written change answers requirement
the pre-preparation flag for due-diligence-class items
the park rule and the automatic conversion to the extension path after the cutoff
excluded: deciding the substantive treatment of anything that arrived
the chase communication itself, owned by the request node
extension client conversation and payment estimate, owned by the extension node

pros.claim: One gate removes the dominant source of rework in a preparation practice, which is starting on an incomplete set
pros.example: a return prepared once, reviewed once and filed, instead of restarted twice as a late document and a corrected statement arrive

pros.claim: Forcing a disposition on absent documents converts an invisible omission risk into a recorded client statement
pros.example: the file showing the client confirmed the rental was sold and no rental statement exists this year, rather than showing nothing at all

cons.claim: The gate holds work that could have started, which feels like idle capacity in a season measured by movement
cons.example: two preparers with clear afternoons while eleven returns sit parked on one missing document each

cons.claim: Strictly applied, the gate pushes clients into extensions they experience as the practice being slow rather than careful
cons.example: a client who sent nine of ten documents on time and hears their return is now an extension

failure_modes: starting 'just the wage part' of a return to look busy and re-touching it three times
letting a preparer wave through an outstanding item without recording the decision
parking returns without an owner or an age, so the parked list becomes a graveyard
asking due-diligence questions after preparation, when the client has stopped answering the phone
acceptance_tests: no return enters preparation with an expected item in the outstanding state and no documented proceed decision
every not-applicable disposition records the client's stated reason
the parked list shows a blocker, an owner and an age for every return on it
returns still parked at the documents-in cutoff appear on the extension conversion list
revisit_triggers: the parked list grows faster than it clears
review or filing keeps discovering documents that intake believed were complete
a season's extension volume departs sharply from what capacity planning assumed

base.update_signal: defect-log evidence that documents keep surfacing after the gate, a parked list that stops clearing, or a shift in the practice's extension volume

nodes.definition: Run the season as a queue with declared states and limits rather than as a pile of folders and a shared anxiety. Every return sits in exactly one state - awaiting documents, ready to prepare, in preparation, awaiting review, awaiting client response, ready to file, transmitted awaiting acknowledgment, closed - and each state has an owner and an age visible to everyone. The number of returns allowed in preparation at one time is capped, because half-finished returns are the practice's inventory and inventory in a compressed season is pure cost: each one has to be re-read, re-oriented and re-checked every time it is picked back up. Triage batches like with like so that concentration is not spent on switching - straightforward wage-and-standard-deduction returns run in a fast lane, self-employment, rental, multi-state and equity-compensation returns are scheduled into blocks with the reviewer capacity they need, and any return whose complexity is unknown is assessed before a date is promised. The throughput mechanism this node encodes is not speed per return; it is fewer restarts, fewer context switches, fewer returns open at once, and an ageing board that shows exactly where the season is actually stuck.

included: the state machine, ownership and ageing
the work-in-progress cap and its rationale
batching and lane assignment by complexity class
assessing unknown-complexity returns before promising dates
excluded: how much total capacity the season should have and how it is staffed and priced
smoothing work into the off-season as a revenue strategy
the review depth decision itself, owned by the tiering node

pros.claim: A capped work-in-progress list finishes more returns per week than an uncapped one because nothing is re-read three times
pros.example: a preparer who keeps four returns open and closes them finishing ahead of one juggling twelve

pros.claim: Batching by complexity preserves the concentration that complex returns need and lets simple ones run at speed
pros.example: self-employment returns scheduled into morning blocks while afternoon runs the wage-income fast lane

pros.claim: An ageing board makes the true bottleneck visible instead of assumed
pros.example: discovering that returns wait longest in awaiting-client-response, not in preparation, and reallocating a person to chasing

cons.claim: Work-in-progress caps mean telling clients no or later during the weeks they most want yes
cons.example: a walk-in in the final fortnight told the realistic date is after the deadline, on the extension path

cons.claim: Maintaining states and ages is overhead that decays fastest exactly when the season is heaviest
cons.example: a board last updated on Tuesday being used to make Friday's promises

failure_modes: measuring the season by returns started rather than returns closed
letting every preparer keep their own private queue and priorities
promising completion dates for returns whose complexity has not been assessed
letting the board go stale so decisions are made on remembered status
acceptance_tests: every open return has exactly one state, one owner and a visible age
the work-in-progress cap is stated and the board shows when it is exceeded
no completion date is promised for a return whose complexity class has not been assessed
revisit_triggers: a state's ageing distribution moves sharply between weeks
review or filing becomes the constraint rather than preparation
staffing changes mid-season

base.update_signal: week-over-week ageing data showing the constraint has moved between states, or a season where returns closed per preparer-week diverges from the plan

nodes.definition: Prepare so that every figure on the return traces to a specific document or a recorded client statement, and leave that trail behind in a form a second person can follow at speed. Concretely the standard requires: an index of the documents relied on; a tie-out in both directions, so each entered figure has a document behind it and each received document has been entered somewhere or marked deliberately not applicable; a judgment note for every call that was not mechanical, stating the fact assumed, the document supporting it, the authority rung reached and who decided; an explicit record of the question asked and the answer given wherever a number rests on a client statement rather than a form, in the client's own words; and a flag rather than a silent guess wherever the preparer is unsure, which is the mechanism that feeds the ambiguity protocol instead of burying the doubt. The standard is justified by its consumers: the reviewer, the due-diligence record, a future notice response, next year's baseline and, in the worst case, a claim file all read the same trail, and reconstructing it months later from memory and a client's recollection costs several times what recording it once during preparation does.

included: the document index and the two-directional tie-out
the judgment note form and the client statement record
the flag-do-not-guess rule that routes doubt to the ambiguity protocol
excluded: the substantive treatment decisions themselves
the due-diligence-specific record class, which has its own node and obligations
software configuration and diagnostics, held by the diagnostics node

pros.claim: A two-directional tie-out is the cheapest control that catches both transcription and omission, the two highest-frequency error classes
pros.example: a document received in January, indexed and never entered, surfacing at tie-out rather than in a matching notice a year later

pros.claim: Judgment notes make review fast because the reviewer checks a stated position rather than reverse-engineering the preparer's reasoning
pros.example: a reviewer confirming a stated home-office assumption in a minute instead of re-deriving it from the return

cons.claim: Workpaper discipline is the first thing abandoned under deadline pressure, precisely when it is most needed
cons.example: a late-March batch prepared with no notes because the preparer intended to add them after the deadline

cons.claim: Over-documenting simple returns burns capacity with no error reduction to show for it
cons.example: three notes on a single-employer wage return where the tie-out alone was sufficient

failure_modes: entering a figure from a document that is not in the index
recording a client's answer as a conclusion rather than as their statement
guessing quietly on an unclear item instead of raising the flag
leaving notes to be written after the season, when the facts have faded
acceptance_tests: every entered figure traces to an indexed document or a recorded client statement, and every indexed document is entered or marked not applicable with a reason
every non-mechanical decision on the return has a note naming the fact, the support, the authority rung and the decision-maker
unresolved items appear as flags routed to the ambiguity protocol, not as completed entries
revisit_triggers: review returns corrections that the workpapers should have prevented
a notice response requires facts the file cannot supply
a new return type enters the practice whose judgment calls are unfamiliar

base.update_signal: review corrections or notice responses that trace to missing trail rather than to a wrong decision, or a new return type whose judgment calls the standard does not cover

nodes.definition: Use the preparation software's diagnostics, validations and electronic-filing schema checks as a first-pass control while holding a clear-eyed inventory of what they can and cannot see. They are genuinely reliable on structural and arithmetic defects: missing required fields, identifier and name-control mismatches, internally inconsistent entries, out-of-range values, and the schema violations that would otherwise come back as a transmission reject. The practice therefore clears diagnostics to zero before a return goes to review, or records a reasoned override naming who overrode and why. What diagnostics cannot see is the whole class of defects that matter most: whether the right documents were entered at all, whether income landed on the right schedule, whether a filing status or dependent claim is supportable, whether a carryforward came across correctly, whether the software's own rollover silently dropped something, and whether the client's stated facts are true. The node therefore fixes one rule - a clean diagnostic report is a precondition for review, never a substitute for it - and maintains a short living list of the settings, rollover behaviours and vendor updates that have silently produced wrong returns in this practice's own history.

included: what diagnostics reliably catch and what they are structurally blind to
the clear-to-zero-or-override-with-reason rule
the practice's own list of settings and rollover behaviours that have caused defects
excluded: choosing the preparation software, owned by the practice-setup KB
the electronic-filing credential and infrastructure itself
the human review pass, which is a separate node

pros.claim: Clearing diagnostics before review protects scarce reviewer attention for the defects only a person can find
pros.example: a reviewer spending their pass on schedule classification rather than on a missing identifier the software already flagged

pros.claim: A practice-specific list of known software traps converts painful one-off discoveries into a permanent control
pros.example: a rollover behaviour that once dropped a carryforward becoming a standing check on every affected return

cons.claim: Clean diagnostics create a powerful false sense of completion, which is the exact feeling that skips review
cons.example: a return with all income on the wrong schedule passing every validation and looking finished

cons.claim: Diagnostic noise trains preparers to override without reading, so the control decays into a habit
cons.example: informational messages that appear on nearly every return being cleared reflexively along with a real one

failure_modes: treating a clean diagnostic run as a review
overriding diagnostics without recording who and why
assuming a mid-season software update changed nothing
trusting rollover because the software performed it
acceptance_tests: no return reaches review with uncleared diagnostics or with an override lacking a recorded reason and owner
the practice's known-software-trap list exists, is dated, and is checked when the vendor issues a significant update
revisit_triggers: a vendor update or mid-season release
a defect that diagnostics should plausibly have caught but did not
a reject code pattern that traces to a software setting

base.update_signal: a software release note, a defect that passed clean diagnostics, or a reject pattern traced to a configuration or rollover behaviour

nodes.definition: Maintain a named taxonomy of the ways a return goes wrong, each paired with the stage that produces it and the control that is supposed to catch it, because a practice that cannot name its errors cannot tune its controls. The classes are: omission - a document that exists was never provided or never entered, produced at intake, caught by prior-year reconciliation and the two-directional tie-out; transcription - right document, wrong figure, wrong box or transposed digits, produced in preparation, caught by tie-out and second-person review; classification - income or expense on the wrong schedule or form family, or the wrong treatment of an activity, produced in preparation, caught by review and the ambiguity protocol; status and dependent errors - filing status, dependency, support and residency claims, produced at intake, caught by documented client questions and the due-diligence record; carryforward errors - prior-year figures lost, duplicated or mis-rolled, produced at rollover, caught by baseline comparison; calculation and configuration errors - software settings, elections, allocations between spouses, states or entities, produced in preparation, caught by diagnostics plus year-over-year reasonableness comparison; jurisdictional errors - a required state or local filing missed, or residency allocated wrongly, produced at intake, caught by the change questions; and process errors - authorization unsigned, return untransmitted, acknowledgment unconfirmed, retention incomplete, produced at filing, caught by the filing and closure gates. The taxonomy is the practice's shared vocabulary, the index of the review checklist and the coding scheme of the defect log.

included: the named error classes with producing stage and catching control
its use as the review checklist index and defect-log coding scheme
the distinction between a defect of fact and a defect of process
excluded: the correct treatment that would have avoided a classification error in a specific case
penalty exposure amounts or agency enforcement statistics
staff performance management, which the defect log addresses as control tuning rather than blame

pros.claim: Named classes let the practice see that its problem is one class rather than general carelessness, which is the only actionable finding
pros.example: a season where most escaped defects are carryforward errors, pointing at rollover reconciliation rather than at preparer attention

pros.claim: Pairing each class with a catching control exposes controls that catch nothing and gaps that nothing catches
pros.example: discovering that jurisdictional errors have no control before the change questions were added to the request

cons.claim: Any taxonomy mis-sorts real defects that belong to two classes at once, and mis-sorted data misdirects tuning
cons.example: a missing state filing that was really an omission at intake being logged as a jurisdictional error and blamed on the preparer

cons.claim: A taxonomy tempts a practice into counting rather than fixing, especially when the counts are small
cons.example: a season's log of nine defects being analysed as if it carried statistical weight

failure_modes: leaving the taxonomy in a document nobody uses at review time
classifying every defect as preparer error, which makes control tuning impossible
letting the classes drift so this season's log cannot be compared to last season's
counting defects caught at review as successes without asking which gate should have caught them
acceptance_tests: every class in the taxonomy names its producing stage and at least one catching control
the review checklist and the defect log both use the taxonomy's class names verbatim
no class exists without a control, and no control exists that catches no class
revisit_triggers: a defect arrives that does not fit any class
a new return type, jurisdiction or reporting form enters the practice
the same class keeps being caught at a later stage than the one that owns it

base.update_signal: a logged defect that fits no existing class, or a season's log showing a class consistently caught downstream of its owning control

nodes.definition: Treat the credits and filing statuses that carry a paid-preparer due-diligence obligation class - earned-income-type credits, child- and dependent-related credits, education credits, and head-of-household-type status in the regimes that impose it, with the current scope, forms, questions and retention requirements to be verified in the practice's own jurisdiction - as items where reaching the right answer is only half the obligation, the other half being the practice's ability to show afterwards how it reached it. The record has four parts: the eligibility questions actually asked; the client's answers recorded in their own terms rather than as the preparer's conclusion; the documents the client provided or specifically described, with the fact recorded that they were seen or described rather than assumed; and a contemporaneous note explaining any answer that looked inconsistent with something else in the file and how it was resolved. Two habits make this survive peak season: asking and recording at intake, when the client is present and engaged, rather than reconstructing at review when they have stopped answering the phone; and refusing to complete a due-diligence-class item on a verbal yes the file cannot evidence, however long the client has been with the practice.

included: the four-part record and its contemporaneous requirement
the intake-time asking habit and the no-verbal-yes rule
the obligation class named with a verify-locally instruction
excluded: stating any jurisdiction's current eligibility tests, forms, penalty amounts or retention periods
deciding a specific client's eligibility
the wider workpaper standard, which this record sits inside

pros.claim: A record built at intake is the only version of this evidence that exists when it is later needed
pros.example: a residency and support question answered and written down in February being available when the file is reviewed a year later

pros.claim: The inconsistency note is where the obligation actually bites, and having a fixed place for it stops preparers from silently choosing the convenient reading
pros.example: an address on a document that does not match the claimed household being questioned and resolved in writing rather than passed over

cons.claim: The record is real time per return, concentrated on exactly the client segment least able to pay a larger fee
cons.example: additional documented questions on a straightforward household return whose fee cannot absorb them

cons.claim: Documented questioning can feel to a long-standing client like an accusation, and handling that badly costs the relationship
cons.example: a client of many years asked for the first time to evidence a dependent's residency and reading it as distrust

failure_modes: completing the record from the preparer's assumptions rather than the client's answers
asking the questions but recording only the conclusion
accepting a verbal assurance because the client is well known to the practice
reconstructing the record after preparation to satisfy a checklist
acceptance_tests: every due-diligence-class item on a return has all four record parts present and dated to the time the answers were given
any inconsistency between an answer and a document in the file has a written resolution note
the content names the obligation class and instructs verification of current local requirements rather than asserting them
revisit_triggers: the filing year's rules, forms or required questions for these items change
a client's answers change materially from the prior year
a notice or review challenges an item in this class

base.update_signal: a locally verified change in the due-diligence obligation class or its required questions and forms, or a challenged item in this class on a filed return

nodes.definition: Run a fixed procedure the moment a preparer cannot support a treatment from clear authority plus the client's documents, so that doubt becomes a decision instead of a stall or a quiet guess. First, restate the item as a fact pattern rather than a conclusion and name the single fact that would change the answer. Second, timebox research on the authority ladder for the filing year in question, with the box set by the return's tier rather than by the preparer's curiosity. Third, if it is still unresolved when the box closes, choose deliberately and visibly among five options: escalate to the practice's credentialed reviewer; go back to the client for the missing document or a written statement of the fact; refer the client out for the licensed judgment the question actually needs; extend the return so the decision is made with time rather than against the clock; or decline the position and prepare on the supportable basis with the client informed in writing of what was excluded and why. The option that is never available is the sixth one nobody writes down - filing on a hopeful assumption because it is late in the season. Whatever is chosen, the conclusion, the rung reached, the decision-maker and the date go into the workpapers before the return moves on.

included: the fact-pattern restatement and the deciding-fact question
the tier-scaled research timebox
the five named exits and the forbidden sixth
the recorded conclusion with rung, decision-maker and date
excluded: the substantive answer to any question the protocol routes
who the practice's outside credentialed reviewer should be and what they charge
the client-facing extension conversation, owned by the extension node

pros.claim: A timebox plus named exits stops the two failure modes at once - the return that stalls for days and the guess that gets filed
pros.example: an unclear multi-state allocation escalated after twenty minutes instead of absorbing an afternoon or being resolved by intuition

pros.claim: Restating as a fact pattern often dissolves the question by revealing which document is actually missing
pros.example: an unclear business-versus-hobby item turning into a request for the client's activity records rather than a research project

cons.claim: Escalation concentrates the hard items on the one credentialed person, who becomes the season's bottleneck
cons.example: a queue of escalated questions waiting on the single reviewer in the last fortnight

cons.claim: Deferring to an extension is the right call and still costs the practice cash timing and a client conversation it would rather not have
cons.example: a client who expected to be finished in March being told the item needs off-season time

failure_modes: researching without a timebox until the day is gone
escalating without a written fact pattern, so the reviewer starts from nothing
choosing the exit by what is quickest rather than by what the file can support
resolving the item verbally and never writing the conclusion into the workpapers
acceptance_tests: every flagged item has a recorded exit - escalated, returned to client, referred, extended or declined - with a date and a decision-maker
no filed return contains a position whose workpaper note lacks an authority rung
research time on an item is bounded by the box its tier sets, with the overflow going to escalation
revisit_triggers: the same question class recurs across clients and should become a standing position rather than a repeated escalation
escalations exceed the credentialed reviewer's capacity
a filed position from a prior season is challenged

base.update_signal: a recurring question class that should be standardised, escalation volume outrunning reviewer capacity, or a challenge to a position the protocol previously resolved

nodes.definition: Assign each return a review tier before it is prepared, so that review capacity - the scarcest thing in a peak season after preparer hours - is spent where the cost of an error is highest, rather than spread evenly by habit and then abandoned when the queue lengthens. Tiering runs on observable signals rather than impressions: the preparer's experience and whether this is their first return of this type this season; the complexity class (self-employment, rental, multi-state, equity compensation, partnership or corporate schedules, foreign accounts, digital assets, first-year depreciation); the presence of any due-diligence-class credit or status; whether the client is new to the practice or the fact pattern is new to the preparer; large year-over-year swings in income, refund or balance due; and any flag raised by the ambiguity protocol. Tiers run from documented self-check, through second-person review, to full credentialed review of the return, its workpapers and its authority notes. The rule that protects the season is asymmetric on purpose: any person may raise a return's tier, and only the credentialed reviewer may lower one - never the calendar, never the client's impatience, and never the preparer who prepared it.

included: the risk signals that set the tier and when they are evaluated
the tier ladder from self-check to credentialed review
the raise-by-anyone, lower-by-reviewer-only asymmetry
excluded: the contents of the review pass itself
hiring, training and compensating reviewers
pricing the additional review time into the fee

pros.claim: Tiering concentrates the reviewer on the returns whose errors are expensive instead of rationing attention at random
pros.example: every first-year depreciation return getting credentialed eyes while single-employer wage returns run on documented self-check

pros.claim: Setting the tier before preparation means the review capacity is scheduled rather than discovered
pros.example: the reviewer's week planned around the tiered returns already in the queue rather than around whatever arrives

cons.claim: Signals are proxies, and a simple-looking return can hide the season's worst error
cons.example: a wage-only return with an unnoticed state residency change routed to the fast lane

cons.claim: The asymmetric rule creates visible friction with the person under the most time pressure, usually the owner
cons.example: the owner-preparer wanting to self-clear a tier-three return at eight in the evening and having to wait

failure_modes: assigning tiers after preparation, when the reviewer's time is already committed
letting the preparer set their own tier
silently downgrading tiers in the final fortnight
never revisiting the signal list even as the client mix changes
acceptance_tests: every return carries a tier assigned before preparation began, with the signals that produced it recorded
no tier was lowered by anyone other than the credentialed reviewer, and every lowering has a reason
escaped defects are checked against tier to see whether the signal set missed them
revisit_triggers: an escaped defect on a return that was tiered low
reviewer capacity is consistently over- or under-subscribed
the client mix or return-type mix shifts between seasons

base.update_signal: escaped-defect data cross-tabulated against assigned tier, or a change in the practice's return-type mix or reviewer capacity

nodes.definition: Execute review as a defined pass that leaves evidence, not as a glance at the refund line and a signature. The pass is indexed by the error taxonomy and runs the same order every time: reconcile the document index against the return so that nothing received went unentered and nothing entered lacks a document; verify tie-out on the highest-value and most error-prone entries rather than on everything; run the year-over-year comparison against the prior-year baseline and require an explanation for every material swing and every item that disappeared; confirm filing status, dependents, residency and the full set of jurisdictions that need returns; verify carryforwards, elections and depreciation continuity against the prior file rather than against the software; confirm diagnostics are clear or overrides are reasoned; confirm the due-diligence record is complete for every item in that class; and read the judgment notes to confirm each carries a fact, a support, an authority rung and a decision-maker. The pass ends in a recorded sign-off naming the reviewer, the tier, what was checked and what was sent back - and a return that comes back from correction is re-reviewed on the corrected points and their neighbours, never assumed fixed because the preparer says so.

included: the ordered checklist indexed to the error classes
the year-over-year comparison and its explanation requirement
the recorded sign-off and the re-review of corrections
excluded: setting the tier, which happens before preparation
the client-facing walkthrough, which is a separate node
performance management of the preparer whose return was corrected

pros.claim: A year-over-year comparison is the single highest-yield review check because it surfaces omissions and carryforward defects that look like nothing on the return itself
pros.example: a retirement distribution present last year and absent this year prompting a question that recovers a document the client forgot

pros.claim: A recorded sign-off makes review auditable and makes skipped review visible rather than deniable
pros.example: the closed file showing the reviewer, the tier and the corrections cycle instead of an unmarked return

cons.claim: Full review of every return is unaffordable in peak weeks, which is exactly why the tier decides depth and why the tier is under constant pressure
cons.example: a reviewer with a day's capacity and two days of tier-three returns in the final week

cons.claim: Reviewers drift toward the checks they personally find interesting and away from the dull ones that catch the most
cons.example: careful attention to a depreciation method while the document reconciliation is skimmed

failure_modes: reviewing the return without opening the workpapers
accepting a corrected return without re-checking the correction
letting review become a second preparation, redoing work instead of checking it
signing off without recording what was checked
acceptance_tests: every filed return carries a sign-off naming reviewer, tier, checks performed and corrections returned
every material year-over-year swing and every disappeared item has a recorded explanation before sign-off
returns that came back from correction show a re-review of the corrected points
revisit_triggers: a defect escapes review and reaches the client or the agency
the same correction is returned repeatedly to the same preparer or across the team
review throughput becomes the season's binding constraint

base.update_signal: escaped defects traced to a check the pass contains but skipped, or defect-log evidence that a checklist item never catches anything

nodes.definition: Walk the client through the finished return before anything is signed, and treat that walkthrough as two things at once: the last and often best omission detector in the pipeline, and the moment the practice's conduct rule is tested in person.
