The walkthrough covers, in the client's language, what the return says - which income sources are included and where each came from, the filing status and dependents claimed, the main deductions and credits with the document behind each, the balance due or refund and the mechanics of how it will move, and any withholding or estimated-payment consequence stated as an observation about their documented facts rather than as planning advice. It closes with the omission question asked directly: is there any income, account, property, dependent or event this year that we have not discussed. Where the client pushes for a different outcome, the conduct rule is applied verbatim rather than negotiated, and the practice does not adjust the return to a desired number. Anything material the client says in this conversation - a newly remembered account, a correction to a dependent's circumstances, a statement of fact a position rests on - goes into the workpapers before the return moves, and if it changes the return, the return goes back through review rather than forward to signature.

included: the walkthrough content and the closing omission question
recording material client statements into the workpapers
the send-it-back rule when the conversation changes the return
applying the conduct rule to in-person outcome pressure
excluded: giving planning advice about next year, which is advice-side and off-season territory
selling additional services during the walkthrough
the authorization and transmission steps themselves

pros.claim: The closing omission question recovers documents and facts that every upstream control missed, because the client is finally looking at their own year in summary
pros.example: a client remembering a small account closed mid-year only when the income list is read back to them

pros.claim: Explaining the return in plain terms is what makes the client's attestation meaningful rather than a signature on something unread
pros.example: a client understanding why their balance due changed before they sign rather than after they receive a bill

cons.claim: Walkthroughs consume the practice's scarcest peak-season commodity, uninterrupted preparer time, and the pressure to shorten them is constant
cons.example: a compressed five-minute version in the final week that skips the omission question entirely

cons.claim: The conversation is where clients push hardest, so it is the highest-friction point in the pipeline for the practice's conduct rule
cons.example: a client comparing their refund unfavourably to a relative's and asking what can be changed

failure_modes: reading the refund figure and asking for a signature
answering an advice-side question conversationally because the client is already sitting there
capturing a material client statement verbally and never writing it down
letting a return that changed in the conversation go straight to signature without re-review
acceptance_tests: every walkthrough records that the omission question was asked and what the client answered
any material statement made in the conversation appears in the workpapers before signature
no return that changed materially during the walkthrough was transmitted without returning through review
revisit_triggers: omissions are being discovered after filing that the walkthrough should have surfaced
preparers report skipping the walkthrough under time pressure
a client complaint concerns something they say was never explained

base.update_signal: post-filing omissions that the walkthrough should have caught, or preparer reports that the walkthrough is being compressed away under peak load

nodes.definition: Treat the extension as a quality instrument with its decision rule fixed in advance, so that it is chosen while there is still time to choose it rather than reached for in panic. A return goes to the extension path when documents remain incomplete past the season's documents-in cutoff, when an ambiguity is unresolved and needs research or a credentialed decision the calendar cannot fit, when a corrected or late information document is known to be outstanding, when a new client's prior-year baseline cannot be reconstructed in time, or when accepting the return into the peak queue would push other returns past their own gates. The client conversation is scripted and states the class distinction plainly: an extension of time to file is not an extension of time to pay, so the practice prepares a payment estimate from what is known, tells the client what happens if the estimate falls short in terms of the interest and penalty classes that apply, and instructs them to verify current amounts and deadlines rather than relying on a remembered figure. The extended return then re-enters the pipeline at the same gates with a scheduled date, not a vague promise, and its parked blockers stay owned and aged exactly as they were.

included: the five triggers that route a return to extension
the scripted client conversation and the file-versus-pay class distinction
the payment-estimate step and its verify-current-rules flag
re-entry at the same gates with a scheduled date
excluded: extension-season work as an off-season revenue line and how it is priced and sold - sibling KB territory
computing any specific interest or penalty amount
the substantive resolution of the ambiguity that triggered the extension

pros.claim: A pre-declared rule converts the extension from an admission of failure into a scheduled, explainable decision
pros.example: a client told in March that a missing partnership document puts the return on the extension path, with a date, rather than told in April that it is late

pros.claim: Extending the wrong returns out of the peak queue protects the accuracy of the ones that stay in it
pros.example: the reviewer's final week spent on returns that are complete instead of on one return with an unresolved question

cons.claim: Extensions defer fee collection and shift work into the practice's thinner months, which is a real cash and capacity cost
cons.example: a block of extended returns landing in the same off-season weeks the practice had planned for recovery

cons.claim: Clients hear 'extension' as a problem regardless of the explanation, and a share of them will attribute it to the practice's slowness
cons.example: a client who supplied documents late experiencing the extension as the practice's failure to keep up

failure_modes: deciding on an extension too late to prepare a considered payment estimate
letting the client believe an extension postpones payment obligations
extending without recording the blocker, so the return re-enters the off-season with no memory of why
using extensions as a general overflow valve rather than on the declared triggers
acceptance_tests: every extended return records which declared trigger caused it, its blocker and its scheduled re-entry date
every extension conversation records that the file-versus-pay distinction was explained and a payment estimate provided or explicitly declined by the client
the payment-estimate content instructs the client to verify current rates, deadlines and rules rather than stating them as fixed
revisit_triggers: extension volume moves materially against the prior season
extended returns are re-entering later than their scheduled dates
a trigger keeps firing for the same root cause, which belongs upstream at intake

base.update_signal: season-over-season change in extension volume or in re-entry punctuality, or a trigger whose root cause repeatedly sits upstream at intake

nodes.definition: Close the filing step as an evidence-producing sequence rather than a button press. Obtain the taxpayer's - and where applicable the spouse's - signed electronic-filing authorization for the exact return being transmitted, after the walkthrough and never before the return is final, so that what was signed and what was sent are the same document. Apply the preparer's signature and registration identifiers as the signing-preparer obligation class requires, verifying the current requirements locally rather than assuming last year's. Transmit, and then treat the return as filed only when the acceptance acknowledgment has been received and recorded against the client's file; until then its state is transmitted-awaiting-acknowledgment and it stays on the board. Rejects are a normal event with an owner and a clock: read the code, classify it (identifier or name-control mismatch, a duplicate filing that may signal identity theft, a dependent already claimed elsewhere, a schema or calculation validation), correct or route it, re-obtain authorization if the return changed materially, and re-transmit inside the correction window that applies. Paper-file exceptions, separately transmitted state or local filings, and returns where the client must send a payment each carry their own confirmation step, because a return believed filed but never accepted is the highest-cost silent failure this practice can produce.

included: authorization captured after finalisation and re-captured on material change
the signing-preparer obligation class with a verify-locally flag
acknowledgment as the definition of filed, and the reject triage path
separate confirmation for paper, state and client-payment paths
excluded: obtaining or maintaining the electronic-filing credential itself, owned by the practice-setup KB
any statement of current deadlines, correction windows or transmission rules
post-filing correction of substantive errors, which the correction node owns

pros.claim: Making acknowledgment the definition of filed eliminates the failure that is invisible until a notice arrives months later
pros.example: a rejected transmission caught on the board the next morning rather than found in the summer with the deadline long past

pros.claim: Authorizing only the final return keeps the signed document and the transmitted document identical, which is what the file must show later
pros.example: a figure corrected after review triggering a fresh authorization rather than a transmission the client never actually approved

cons.claim: Chasing authorizations is a real bottleneck when clients are remote and the deadline is close
cons.example: a finished return waiting days on a spouse's signature while the queue behind it ages

cons.claim: Acknowledgment tracking is dull administrative work that decays fastest at the moment of peak volume
cons.example: a batch transmitted on the final evening whose acknowledgments nobody reconciles until the following week

failure_modes: collecting a signature on a draft and transmitting a later version
treating transmission as filing and closing the file
letting a reject sit unowned past its correction window
forgetting that a state or local filing transmits and acknowledges separately
acceptance_tests: every transmitted return has a signed authorization matching the version transmitted
every transmission reconciles to a recorded acknowledgment or to an open reject with an owner and a clock
returns with separate state, local, paper or client-payment components have each component's confirmation recorded
signing-preparer content names the obligation class and instructs local verification rather than asserting current requirements
revisit_triggers: a reject code appears that the practice has not seen before
acknowledgment reconciliation finds a gap
the software or transmission process changes mid-season

base.update_signal: an unreconciled transmission found in the season-end sweep, a new or clustering reject code, or a change in the transmission workflow or authorization mechanism

nodes.definition: Fix what a closed file must contain, how long it lives and how it dies. At closure the file holds the signed engagement letter for that year, the document index and the source documents relied on, the workpapers with tie-out marks and judgment notes, the due-diligence records, the review sign-off, the signed electronic-filing authorization, the transmitted return with its acknowledgment, the record of the copy delivered to the client, and any correspondence that changed something. Retention periods and the preparer copy-retention obligation class differ by jurisdiction, by record type and by form, and they change - so the practice keeps one written retention schedule, verified locally and dated, rather than a set of per-preparer habits and a full cupboard. Disposal is the half that gets forgotten: secure destruction of paper and verified deletion of digital copies when retention ends, applied with the same care the safeguards program demands, including the copies that accumulate on desktops, in email and on the portal. Both halves have a direct operational payoff beyond compliance - next season's baseline, a notice response, and any amendment all start from this file, so a file that was assembled properly is the cheapest asset the practice owns, and one that was not is a liability that keeps accruing.

included: the closed-file contents list
the written, dated, locally verified retention schedule as an obligation class
secure destruction and verified deletion including stray copies
the file as the starting point for next year, notices and amendments
excluded: stating any jurisdiction's current retention periods
the client's own record-keeping obligations beyond telling them they have some
next-year client communication and re-engagement, which is sibling territory

pros.claim: A complete closed file is what makes next season cheap and a notice answerable without reconstruction
pros.example: a depreciation schedule and the year's judgment notes sitting where the next preparer looks first

pros.claim: A written schedule ends the accumulation problem, which is a security exposure and a storage cost at the same time
pros.example: records past retention destroyed on a scheduled date instead of surviving indefinitely in a cupboard and a cloud folder

cons.claim: Assembling the file at closure competes with the next return, so it slips to the end of the season and then to never
cons.example: a set of April files closed in name only, missing their authorization copies and review sign-offs

cons.claim: Destruction is irreversible and the schedule may be wrong for a record type, so an over-eager purge can destroy something still needed
cons.example: prior-year depreciation detail destroyed on schedule and needed for a later basis question

failure_modes: closing a file without the authorization, acknowledgment or sign-off in it
keeping everything forever because deciding is harder than storing
destroying paper while forgetting the digital copies, or the reverse
assuming a remembered retention period rather than a verified, dated schedule
acceptance_tests: a sampled closed file contains every listed component, including authorization, acknowledgment, review sign-off and due-diligence records
a written retention schedule exists, is dated, names its verification source and covers both paper and digital copies
destruction events are recorded, and a spot check finds no stray copies of destroyed records in email, desktops or the portal
revisit_triggers: a locally verified change in retention or copy obligation classes
a notice or amendment finds the file missing something it needed
a storage or portal migration

base.update_signal: a locally verified change in retention or copy-retention obligation classes, a file found deficient when a notice or amendment needed it, or a storage migration

nodes.definition: Decide in advance how the practice behaves when it discovers, or is told, that a filed return is wrong, because the temptation to wait and see is strongest exactly when disclosure is most owed. The rule is disclosure-first and prompt: tell the client in writing what was found, what class of consequence it may carry - additional tax, interest and penalty classes, with amounts and current rules to be verified rather than casually estimated to soothe - what the correction options are (an amended return, a superseding filing where the calendar and the regime allow it, or a response to an agency notice), what the practice will do at its own cost where the error was the practice's, and what requires the client's decision and written authorization. Notices are triaged the same way rather than forwarded with a shrug: read what the agency actually says, reconcile it against the closed file, and separate a practice error from a client-information error from an agency matching artefact before answering anything, then respond inside the stated window. Representation limits tied to credential class are respected and named as an obligation class to verify locally; an error of judgment goes back through the ambiguity protocol rather than being re-decided under pressure; and the practice's own liability-cover class is a question to have settled before the first one of these arrives, not after.

included: the disclosure-first behaviour and its written content
the correction option classes and who authorises what
notice triage and the practice-versus-client-versus-agency separation
representation and liability-cover as obligation classes to verify locally
excluded: amendment work as an off-season revenue line, which is sibling territory
computing specific tax, interest or penalty amounts
representing a client where the credential class does not permit it

pros.claim: Prompt written disclosure is what keeps a correctable error from becoming a trust failure and a complaint
pros.example: a carryforward error found in May disclosed the same week with the correction path and the practice's own cost stated

pros.claim: Triaging a notice against the closed file before responding prevents the practice from conceding something that was actually correct
pros.example: a matching notice answered with the document and workpaper reference that shows the item was reported, rather than with a payment

cons.claim: Disclosure invites blame and sometimes fee refunds or absorbed costs at the moment the practice can least afford them
cons.example: an error surfacing in the middle of the next peak season with the client asking who pays for the correction

cons.claim: The correction path is genuinely uncertain until the agency responds, so a client wanting a definite answer will not get one
cons.example: a client asking exactly what the penalty will be when only the applicable class can honestly be named

failure_modes: waiting to see whether anyone notices
estimating a penalty or interest figure to reassure a client
forwarding a notice to the client without reconciling it to the file
amending on assumption without re-running the unclear item through the ambiguity protocol
acting beyond the representation limits of the practice's credential class
acceptance_tests: every discovered error has a dated written disclosure to the client naming what was found, the option classes and who bears which cost
every notice has a file reconciliation recorded before any response is sent, and a response inside the stated window or a documented reason it was not
no client-facing correction document states a specific penalty, interest or deadline figure as fact rather than directing verification
revisit_triggers: any notice or discovered error, which also feeds the defect log
a change in the practice's credential mix or liability cover
a correction that reveals the same root cause as a previous one

base.update_signal: each notice or discovered error and how it resolved, a change in credential mix or liability cover, or a repeat root cause across corrections

nodes.definition: Log every defect at the moment it is caught rather than at season end, capturing six fields that are cheap then and unrecoverable later: the error class from the taxonomy, the stage that produced it, the stage that caught it, whether it reached the client or the agency, the rework time it cost, and any reject or notice code attached. The log is then read in the off-season to change controls, not to rank preparers. It answers the only questions that improve accuracy and throughput together: which class is most frequent, which is most expensive in rework and relationship cost, which control is catching things too late - a defect caught at review that the completeness gate should have caught is a gate failure, not a review success - which checklist items have caught nothing across a whole season and can be retired, and which returns should have been tiered higher or extended. Revision happens between seasons, when there is time to retrain, re-issue checklists and update the request organizer; mid-season changes are permitted only for a defect actively producing wrong filings, because changing controls under load is itself a source of error.

included: the six fields captured at the moment of catch
the stage-of-origin versus stage-of-catch reading
the off-season revision cycle and the narrow mid-season exception
retiring controls that catch nothing
excluded: staff evaluation, discipline and compensation
off-season revenue lines and capacity smoothing, which are sibling territory
publishing defect data to clients in any form

pros.claim: Capturing the producing stage at the moment of catch is the only way the practice ever learns where its errors are made rather than where they are noticed
pros.example: a season showing most transcription defects originate in returns prepared after the daily cap was exceeded

pros.claim: Retiring checklist items that never catch anything keeps review affordable, which is what keeps review from being skipped
pros.example: dropping three legacy checks that caught nothing in two seasons and adding one that would have caught the year's worst defect

cons.claim: Logging is asked of people at the exact moment they are correcting something and least inclined to write it down
cons.example: a reviewer sending back four corrections in the final week and logging none of them

cons.claim: Small-practice defect counts are too small to support confident inference, so the log guides judgment rather than proving anything
cons.example: two carryforward defects in a season reading as a pattern when they may be coincidence

failure_modes: logging only the defects that escaped, which hides the controls that are working and the ones that are barely coping
using the log as a performance record, after which the logging stops
changing controls mid-season on thin evidence
analysing the log so late that the next season's checklists are already printed
acceptance_tests: every correction returned at review or found after filing has a log entry with all six fields
the off-season revision names each control changed, the log evidence for the change, and who re-trained on it
no control was changed mid-season except under the actively-producing-wrong-filings exception, with that reason recorded
revisit_triggers: a defect escapes to the agency or the client
a season ends and the revision cycle is due
the taxonomy changes or a new return type enters the practice

base.update_signal: a season's log showing a class caught consistently downstream of its owning control, or an escaped defect whose class the log did not anticipate

edges.why_related: the boundary is drawn around the stages the charter defines, so that each stage knows which questions it may answer and which it must route
the conduct rule is the client-facing half of the boundary: once you know what you may not decide, you also know what you may not promise
the engagement letter's exclusions and will-not-sign conditions are the written form of the boundary's advice-side column
the baseline is built only for returns the practice has accepted, and the acceptance decision is what obliges a new client to hand over the prior return
the request is generated from the baseline's expected-document inventory rather than from a generic list
arrivals are logged against the outstanding request list, so the channel's index is meaningless without the request that defines what is expected
the intake channel is the first place the safeguards program is exercised, and its conversion path exists because the program forbids the convenient alternatives
the gate is a computation over the indexed arrivals; without the index it degrades to a preparer's impression
tie-out is only possible against a settled document set; preparing before the gate makes the trail chase a moving target
diagnostics are run against a prepared return and their overrides are recorded in the same workpapers
the due-diligence record is a specialised, higher-obligation section of the workpaper trail and inherits its form
the protocol's research step is a climb up the ladder, and the rung reached is what its recorded conclusion cites
tiering allocates depth against the classes the taxonomy says a return is exposed to
the tier decides who reviews and how deep the pass runs before the pass begins
a cleared diagnostic report is a precondition of the review pass, so the reviewer's time goes to what only a person can catch
the client is walked through a reviewed return, never a draft, so the walkthrough discusses numbers that have already been checked
authorization is captured after the walkthrough so the signed return and the transmitted return are the same document
extend is one of the protocol's five named exits, and the extension rule supplies what that exit does next
the acknowledgment and the signed authorization are components the closed file must contain, so closure cannot precede filing
the correction path only exists for a return that was actually filed, and the acknowledgment record establishes what was filed and when
every disclosed error and answered notice becomes a log entry with its class, its producing stage and its rework cost
retention length and destruction method are bounded by the safeguards program: what is kept must be protected, and what is destroyed must be destroyed everywhere it was copied
the boundary limits which exits the protocol may take: an advice-side question cannot be closed by preparer research alone, however good the research
the walkthrough is where outcome pressure is applied in person, so the conduct rule constrains exactly what may be said and offered there
a return carrying a due-diligence-class item whose record is incomplete is not eligible for transmission, regardless of where it sits in the queue
acceptance decides what may enter the season's queue at all, and the documents-in deadline in the letter is the queue's admission rule
the queue rewards movement and the review pass consumes the scarcest capacity in the practice, so peak weeks push constantly toward shallower review
edges.resolution_rule: review depth is set by the assigned tier and may be raised by anyone but lowered only by the credentialed reviewer; when review capacity cannot serve the tier before the deadline, the return goes to the extension path rather than the review being trimmed

edges.why_related: the gate holds returns out of preparation while the queue and the client both want work started, and idle preparer capacity beside a parked list is uncomfortable in peak season
edges.resolution_rule: the gate holds; capacity freed by parked returns goes to chasing outstanding documents and to complete returns further back in the queue, and parked returns past the documents-in cutoff convert to the extension path rather than being started incomplete

edges.why_related: the walkthrough is where a client's demand for a bigger refund meets the practice's refusal to sell an outcome, with a long relationship and this year's fee both on the table
edges.resolution_rule: the conduct rule dominates without exception: state what the documents support, state exactly what would have to be documented for a different result, put the position in writing, and let the client decide whether to obtain that documentation or take the return elsewhere

edges.why_related: extending defers the fee and pushes work into the practice's thin months, which pulls against accepting and finishing everything inside the season
edges.resolution_rule: accuracy dominates cash timing: when any declared extension trigger is present the return extends, with the payment estimate prepared and the file-versus-pay distinction explained; the acceptance criteria for that return type are revisited afterwards rather than the extension being avoided

edges.why_related: research and escalation stop a return moving while the board is measured by movement, and the escalation queue concentrates on one credentialed person
edges.resolution_rule: research is timeboxed by tier and the overflow escalates immediately; a return awaiting escalation moves to a parked state with an owner and an age so it stops consuming preparer attention, and if escalation cannot clear before the deadline the return extends - filing on assumption is never an available exit

edges.why_related: the quality of the baseline directly determines how much the year-over-year comparison can detect: a thin baseline makes the highest-yield review check nearly blind
uncleared schema and identifier diagnostics are the direct upstream cause of the reject codes that appear after transmission
compromised preparer credentials and taxpayer identity theft surface operationally as duplicate-filing rejects and as refund-destination changes at the filing step
the signed engagement precedes the document request, so the client is asked for identifiers and documents only under an agreed scope and fee basis
sign-off precedes authorization capture, and any change after sign-off sends the return back through review before a signature is sought
the log's stage-of-origin data revises which control owns which class, retires checks that catch nothing, and adds classes the season produced that the taxonomy lacked
defects the review keeps catching that the gate should have caught are gate failures, and they tighten the expected-document list and the change questions for the next wave

both are evidence-trail disciplines with the same shape - question, answer, support, contemporaneous note - differing in that one carries a named regulatory obligation class and the other carries the practice's own standard

conflict_axes.name: peak_throughput_versus_verification_depth
conflict_axes.description: The season's economics reward finishing returns and the practice's survival rewards catching errors, and both draw on the same preparer and reviewer hours in the same eight weeks.
poles: verify every return to its assigned depth
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: let the tier decide depth in advance and let the extension absorb the overflow; buy throughput from fewer restarts and fewer open returns rather than from shallower checking

conflict_axes.name: start_now_versus_complete_document_set
conflict_axes.description: A client who has sent most of their documents wants work to begin, and a preparer with an open afternoon wants to begin it, but a return started incomplete is the practice's main source of rework.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: hold the gate and spend the freed capacity on chasing and on complete returns; convert returns still parked at the documents-in cutoff to the extension path

conflict_axes.name: client_outcome_pressure_versus_documented_position
conflict_axes.description: Clients arrive with an expected refund, a relative's result or a former preparer's position, and the practice's answer is bounded by what their documents actually support.
poles: keep the client happy this season
sign only what the file supports
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: apply the conduct script verbatim, state in writing what would have to be documented for a different result, and accept losing the client rather than the position

conflict_axes.name: in_season_revenue_versus_extension_quality
conflict_axes.description: Every extension moves a fee out of the peak weeks and work into the practice's thin months, while every rushed return raises the chance of a correction that costs more than the fee.
poles: extend it and decide with time
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: treat the declared extension triggers as binding, prepare the payment estimate early, and address the cash consequence through acceptance criteria and scheduling rather than by overriding the trigger

conflict_axes.name: software_confidence_versus_human_verification
conflict_axes.description: A clean diagnostic report feels like a finished return, and it is genuinely evidence about one narrow class of defect and no evidence at all about the classes that cause notices.
poles: verify by hand against documents and the prior year
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: require diagnostics clear as a precondition of review and forbid them as a substitute for it; keep a written list of what the software cannot see

conflict_axes.name: client_convenience_versus_data_protection
conflict_axes.description: The easiest way for a client to send a document is the least safe way, and insisting on the safe channel costs responsiveness with exactly the clients least able to use it.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep the single channel as the rule and invest in a documented conversion path plus assisted onboarding for clients who cannot use it, rather than quietly tolerating unsafe delivery

conflict_axes.name: answer_the_question_versus_stay_in_lane
conflict_axes.description: Clients ask advice-side questions casually and in the moment, and the most helpful-feeling response is the one that crosses the boundary between preparation and personalized advice.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: route visibly with a named next step and a date, so the client experiences movement rather than refusal, and keep any written answer inside the preparation column

conflict_axes.name: documentation_cost_versus_defensibility
conflict_axes.description: Every note, question and record costs minutes on a fixed per-return fee, and the file's ability to answer a notice or a due-diligence enquiry a year later depends entirely on those minutes having been spent.
poles: document as if it will be examined
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: scale the trail to the item, not to the return: full record for due-diligence-class items and judgment calls, tie-out only for mechanical entries

conflict_axes.name: disclose_the_error_versus_protect_the_practice
conflict_axes.description: When the practice finds its own error after filing, prompt written disclosure is owed and every instinct - reputational, financial, seasonal - argues for waiting to see whether it matters.
poles: wait and see whether it surfaces
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: disclosure-first is absolute; describe consequence classes rather than invented figures, state what the practice will bear, and route the root cause to the defect log rather than to a private resolution

edge_cases.description: A corrected information document arrives from the client's broker after the return has been transmitted but before the filing deadline
edge_cases.trigger: a corrected or amended information document supersedes one already used on a filed return
edge_cases.mitigation: index the corrected document, reconcile it against what was filed, tell the client in writing what changed and what the correction options are, and decide between a superseding filing where the calendar and regime allow one and an amended return - never leave the difference unaddressed because the return is already accepted

edge_cases.description: The return rejects because a dependent has already been claimed on another filed return
edge_cases.trigger: a dependent-claimed reject code returns after transmission
edge_cases.mitigation: do not re-transmit with the claim removed to clear the reject; go back to the documented residency and support answers, ask the client what they know about the other filing, record the conversation, and route the entitlement question through the ambiguity protocol - the paper-filing and dispute path is a class to verify currently rather than assume

edge_cases.description: A return rejects as a duplicate filing for a taxpayer who has not filed, suggesting the identity was used by someone else
edge_cases.trigger: a duplicate-filing reject on a client the practice knows has not filed
edge_cases.mitigation: treat it as a suspected identity-theft event: tell the client the same day, follow the identity-theft reporting and protective-filing obligation classes after verifying their current requirements, check whether the exposure could have originated in the practice, and log it as an incident rather than as a routine reject

edge_cases.description: A client of many years insists on a deduction the file cannot substantiate and says the practice has always allowed it
edge_cases.trigger: a long-standing client asserts a position with no current-year substantiation and applies relationship pressure
edge_cases.mitigation: run the conduct script, state precisely what documentation would support the position and how to produce it, prepare on the supportable basis with the exclusion confirmed in writing, and if the client insists, decline the position and let them take the return elsewhere with the practice's position recorded

edge_cases.description: A client's answer to a due-diligence eligibility question contradicts a document already in their file
edge_cases.trigger: an inconsistency between a stated answer and an indexed document on a due-diligence-class item
edge_cases.mitigation: stop, ask the follow-up question, record the client's answer in their own words and the resolution note that reconciles it, and do not complete the item on a verbal assurance the file cannot evidence; where it cannot be reconciled, the item is not claimed

edge_cases.description: A new client cannot produce a prior-year return or the depreciation schedule for a rental they have owned for years
edge_cases.trigger: prior-year baseline unobtainable at intake for a return with carryforward-dependent items
edge_cases.mitigation: make the explicit decision at intake rather than mid-preparation: reconstruct with the client's records and price it as such, limit the engagement in writing, extend so reconstruction has time, or decline - and never carry forward a figure the file cannot source

edge_cases.description: A partnership or trust information document is known to be outstanding as the deadline approaches
edge_cases.trigger: a pass-through information document has not been issued and cannot be obtained before the deadline
edge_cases.mitigation: route to the extension path on the declared trigger, prepare the payment estimate from what is known, explain the file-versus-pay distinction with an instruction to verify current amounts and dates, and schedule the re-entry date rather than promising to watch for the document

edge_cases.description: A client emails photographs of documents containing identifiers to a preparer's personal address because the portal was inconvenient
edge_cases.trigger: sensitive client data arrives outside the indexed secure channel
edge_cases.mitigation: run the conversion path once - move the items into the index, confirm legibility and year, delete the insecure copies including from sent items and device storage - then tell the client plainly why the channel exists and help them onto it rather than accepting the pattern

edge_cases.description: A message that imitates the software vendor or the tax agency asks a preparer to re-enter electronic-filing credentials mid-season
edge_cases.trigger: a credential-harvesting attempt targeting the practice during peak weeks
edge_cases.mitigation: no credential is ever entered from a link; verify through the known vendor channel, rotate credentials if there is any doubt, check the filing account for transmissions the practice did not make, and follow the account-compromise reporting obligation class after verifying its current requirements

edge_cases.description: Mid-preparation it emerges that the client worked in another state and a filing the practice does not handle is required
edge_cases.trigger: a jurisdiction outside the practice's competence surfaces after acceptance
edge_cases.mitigation: stop and re-run acceptance for the added jurisdiction: refer that filing out with a written scope change, or extend so it can be handled properly, and record the change question that failed to surface it so intake catches the pattern next time

edge_cases.description: A seasonal preparer's returns show the same classification defect appearing repeatedly late in the season
edge_cases.trigger: a defect pattern concentrated in one preparer or one return type after peak load began
edge_cases.mitigation: raise the tier for that preparer's affected return type immediately, re-review the already-filed returns in that pattern for the same defect, and record it as a control and training finding rather than as a personnel verdict

edge_cases.description: A finished, reviewed return cannot be signed because one spouse is unreachable as the deadline arrives
edge_cases.trigger: authorization cannot be obtained before the filing deadline on a completed return
edge_cases.mitigation: never transmit on a partial or assumed authorization; move the return to the extension path with a payment estimate, document the attempts to reach the client, and keep the reviewed return ready so filing follows immediately once the signature exists

workflow.action: Charter the per-return pipeline and its definition of done
workflow.description: Write the ordered stage list, the gate each stage must satisfy, and the rule that a return which cannot pass its gate is parked or extended rather than pushed forward
workflow.artifact: written pipeline charter with stage list, gates and definition of done
workflow.gate: the stage list, its gates and a definition of done ending at logged acknowledgment plus complete file are written and reflected on the queue board

workflow.action: Draw the preparation-versus-advice boundary and publish the routing wording
workflow.description: Classify the question types the practice actually receives into preparation-side and advice-side, attach the routing wording to the advice side, and flag credential and representation requirements as obligation classes to verify locally
workflow.artifact: two-column question classification with routing script and obligation-class flags
workflow.gate: every recurring question type is classified, the routing wording is written, and no content asserts a current jurisdictional requirement

workflow.action: Stand up the client-data safeguards program before any documents arrive
workflow.description: Put the written information security program, access control, multi-factor authentication, vendor due-diligence, training and the incident path in place and check them before the season opens
workflow.artifact: dated written information security program with an access list and an incident path
workflow.gate: the program names a responsible person, multi-factor authentication is verified on filing, portal and email accounts, and the incident path names the first three actions

workflow.action: Screen the return and sign the engagement scope
workflow.description: Apply the competence, capacity, records and posture tests, then record the accept, refer or decline decision and issue the engagement letter with exclusions, fee basis and the documents-in deadline
workflow.artifact: signed engagement letter and recorded acceptance decision
workflow.gate: no work has begun without a signed letter for the year, and the acceptance record names which test the decision turned on

workflow.action: Reconstruct the prior-year baseline and issue the personalized document request
workflow.description: Extract the expected-document inventory, the household picture, the carryforward inventory and the recurring judgment items, then generate the client's document request and change questions from them
workflow.artifact: baseline sheet with carryforward inventory plus the issued document request
workflow.gate: every expected document is named by form family and source, and every carryforward item has a prior-year source recorded

workflow.action: Receive documents through the indexed channel and hold the completeness gate
workflow.description: Log arrivals against the request list, run the arrival checks, obtain written change answers, flag due-diligence-class items, and give every expected-but-absent item a disposition before preparation may start
workflow.artifact: reconciled completeness sheet with dispositions and the parked list
workflow.gate: no expected item sits outstanding without a documented proceed decision, change answers are in writing, and parked returns carry a blocker, an owner and an age

workflow.action: Triage the return into the queue with a state, a lane and a review tier
workflow.description: Place the return in exactly one state with an owner, assign its complexity lane and its review tier from the risk signals, and respect the work-in-progress cap before anything is started
workflow.artifact: queue board entry with state, owner, lane, tier and age
workflow.gate: the return has one state, one owner, an assessed complexity class and a tier assigned before preparation begins

workflow.action: Prepare the return against the workpaper standard
workflow.description: Enter from indexed documents with two-directional tie-out, record client statements verbatim where a figure rests on one, complete the due-diligence records, and raise flags rather than guesses on unclear items
workflow.artifact: prepared return with document index, tie-out marks, judgment notes and due-diligence records
workflow.gate: every figure traces to a document or a recorded statement, every document is entered or excluded with a reason, and unclear items are flagged rather than resolved silently

workflow.action: Resolve every flagged ambiguity through the triage protocol
workflow.description: Restate each flag as a fact pattern, timebox the research on the authority ladder for the filing year, then take one of the five named exits and write the conclusion into the workpapers
workflow.artifact: conclusion notes with authority rung, exit taken, decision-maker and date
workflow.gate: no flag remains open, no exit is 'assumed', and every conclusion names its rung and decision-maker

workflow.action: Review at the assigned tier and record the sign-off
workflow.description: Run the taxonomy-indexed checklist including the document reconciliation, the year-over-year comparison, the status and jurisdiction check, carryforward continuity, diagnostics and the due-diligence records, then sign off and re-review any corrections
workflow.artifact: recorded review sign-off with checks performed and corrections returned
workflow.gate: diagnostics are clear or overridden with reason, every material year-over-year swing is explained, and the sign-off names reviewer, tier and corrections

workflow.action: Walk the client through the return, capture authorization, transmit and confirm acknowledgment
workflow.description: Explain the return in the client's language and ask the omission question, apply the conduct rule to any outcome pressure, obtain signed authorization for the final version, transmit, and track to acceptance or to an owned reject
workflow.artifact: signed authorization, transmission record and logged acknowledgment
workflow.gate: the signed authorization matches the transmitted version, the omission question and its answer are recorded, and the return is not treated as filed until the acknowledgment is logged

workflow.action: Close the file, apply the retention schedule and log the season's defects
workflow.description: Assemble the closed file with every required component, apply the dated retention schedule to paper and digital copies alike, and enter each defect caught during the return into the log with its producing and catching stages
workflow.artifact: closed client file plus defect log entries
workflow.gate: the file contains engagement letter, document index, workpapers, due-diligence records, sign-off, authorization, return and acknowledgment, and every correction from this return has a log entry

dominance_rules.rationale: a filing deadline is recoverable through an extension while a wrong filed return costs the client money and the practice its standing
dominance_rules.trigger: a stage gate cannot be satisfied before the deadline
dominance_rules.action: park or extend the return; never advance a return past a gate it has not passed

dominance_rules.rule: The conduct rule dominates client outcome pressure and retention risk
dominance_rules.rationale: a signature on an unsupportable position is the one loss a practice cannot undo, and outcome selling attracts exactly the clients who produce them
dominance_rules.trigger: a client demands a larger refund, compares another preparer's result, or asks for a position the file cannot support
dominance_rules.action: deliver the scripted response, put the position and what would change it in writing, and let the client decide whether to obtain documentation or leave

dominance_rules.rule: Data protection dominates client and staff convenience
dominance_rules.rationale: the practice holds the household's whole identity and a breach cannot be walked back or apologised away
dominance_rules.trigger: any request to send, store or access client data outside the indexed secure channel or the access rules
dominance_rules.action: refuse the shortcut, run the documented conversion path, and record the exception

dominance_rules.rule: A complete due-diligence record dominates transmission
dominance_rules.rationale: the obligation attaches to the practice regardless of how long the client has been coming and regardless of the queue
dominance_rules.trigger: a return carries a due-diligence-class item whose four-part record is incomplete
dominance_rules.action: hold transmission, obtain the questions, answers and support, and record the resolution before the return moves

dominance_rules.rule: The credentialed reviewer dominates on advice-side judgment
dominance_rules.rationale: the classification exists precisely because these questions exceed what preparation-side work may decide
dominance_rules.trigger: an advice-side question or an unresolved treatment reaches a preparer
dominance_rules.action: route it - escalate, refer or return to the client for facts - and never close it with preparer research alone

dominance_rules.rule: Acknowledgment dominates the belief that a return was sent
dominance_rules.rationale: a transmitted return that was never accepted is invisible until it becomes expensive
dominance_rules.trigger: a transmission has no logged acceptance within the expected window
dominance_rules.action: keep the return on the board in transmitted-awaiting-acknowledgment, assign the reject an owner and a clock, and never close the file on a transmission alone

dominance_rules.rule: Assigned review tier dominates schedule pressure
dominance_rules.rationale: tiering is the mechanism that spends scarce review where errors are expensive, and it only works if it cannot be quietly relaxed
dominance_rules.trigger: anyone proposes reducing review depth to meet a date
dominance_rules.action: keep the tier; anyone may raise it, only the credentialed reviewer may lower it, and if the tier cannot be served in time the return extends

dominance_rules.rule: The completeness gate dominates queue movement
dominance_rules.rationale: starting incomplete is the practice's largest single source of rework and of returns touched three times
dominance_rules.trigger: a return is available to start but an expected document is outstanding without a documented decision
dominance_rules.action: park it with a blocker and an owner, work the chase list, and start a complete return instead

dominance_rules.rule: Disclosure dominates self-protection when an error is found
dominance_rules.rationale: the client's exposure grows with silence and the practice's exposure grows faster
dominance_rules.trigger: the practice discovers or is told that a filed return is wrong
dominance_rules.action: disclose in writing promptly with the option classes and the practice's own cost stated, name consequence classes rather than invented figures, and log the root cause

dominance_rules.rationale: mid-season goodwill work becomes unbilled obligation and unowned risk
dominance_rules.trigger: a client asks mid-engagement for prior-year work, an amendment, bookkeeping, a notice response or another jurisdiction
dominance_rules.action: issue a written scope change with its own fee basis and acceptance test, or refer it out

anti_rework_rules.rule: Reconstruct the prior-year baseline before issuing the document request
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a generic request that misses carryforwards and payer-specific documents and reopens intake after preparation has started

anti_rework_rules.rule: Sign the engagement letter before any preparation work begins
anti_rework_rules.prevents: scope arguments at billing and unpaid rework on work nobody agreed to

anti_rework_rules.rule: Hold the completeness gate before preparation rather than after
anti_rework_rules.prevents: returns touched three and four times and reviewed against a document set that keeps changing

anti_rework_rules.rule: Ask and record due-diligence questions at intake, while the client is engaged
anti_rework_rules.prevents: reconstructing eligibility evidence at review week from a client who has stopped answering the phone

anti_rework_rules.rule: Assign the review tier before preparation, not after
anti_rework_rules.prevents: discovering at review that a return needed credentialed attention nobody had scheduled

anti_rework_rules.rule: Clear software diagnostics before handing a return to review
anti_rework_rules.prevents: reviewers spending their scarce pass on machine-detectable defects and correction cycles that add a day each

anti_rework_rules.rule: Decide the extension while there is still time to prepare a payment estimate
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a rushed filing, an unadvised balance due, and a client conversation held after the deadline instead of before it

anti_rework_rules.rule: Capture the authorization only after the return is final and re-capture it on material change
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a signed draft that differs from the transmitted return and a second signature chase at the worst moment

anti_rework_rules.rule: Confirm the acknowledgment before the file is closed and the return leaves the board
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a silently unfiled or rejected return discovered months later with the deadline gone

anti_rework_rules.rule: Log each defect at the moment it is caught, with its producing stage
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an off-season review that can count defects but cannot say where they were made, and therefore cannot fix a control

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect reaches the client or the agency
iteration_protocol.action: root-cause it to the stage that should have caught it, tighten that control rather than the one that found it, and re-check other returns exposed to the same class

iteration_protocol.trigger: electronic-filing rejects cluster on one code
iteration_protocol.action: trace the code to its producing step, fix the setting, entry habit or data check that causes it, and add it to the known-traps list

iteration_protocol.trigger: the parked list ages past the season's documents-in cutoff
iteration_protocol.action: convert the affected returns to the extension path as a batch with scripted client conversations and payment estimates, and stop spending peak capacity chasing them individually

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new filing year's forms, instructions and rules are published
iteration_protocol.action: re-verify every conclusion the practice carries forward, update the organizer and change questions, refresh the checklists and retrain before the season opens

iteration_protocol.trigger: a phishing attempt, credential compromise, vendor breach notice or suspected identity-theft reject appears
iteration_protocol.action: run the incident path, rotate credentials, check the filing account for transmissions the practice did not make, and re-verify the notification obligation classes locally

iteration_protocol.trigger: review keeps returning the same correction to the same preparer or the same return type
iteration_protocol.action: raise the tier for that pattern immediately, re-check already-filed returns in the pattern, and schedule the training as a control change rather than a personnel matter

iteration_protocol.trigger: a notice arrives or a client reports an agency contact about a return the practice prepared
iteration_protocol.action: reconcile the notice against the closed file before responding, separate practice error from client-information error from agency artefact, and feed whatever it reveals into the workpaper standard and the log

iteration_protocol.trigger: an accepted return type repeatedly consumes far more effort than its acceptance assessment predicted
iteration_protocol.action: revisit the acceptance criteria, the complexity lane and the charter's stage assumptions for that type before the next season rather than absorbing the overrun again

priority_rationale: The frame nodes come first because every later decision depends on knowing what one finished return is, which questions the practice may answer at all, what it may never promise, what counts as authority, and how the client's data is protected; intake nodes follow because the prior-year baseline, the personalized request, the secure indexed channel and the completeness gate are what make a return preparable exactly once; production and control nodes sit in the middle because tie-out workpapers, diagnostics, the error taxonomy, the due-diligence record and the ambiguity protocol are the controls that let peak throughput rise without accuracy falling; and review, filing, retention and defect tuning come last because they close the loop - depth allocated by tier, filing proven by acknowledgment, the file assembled for next year and a notice, and the season's defects turned into next season's controls.
